hypothesis: Which profilers work inside the P1 Lambda (python3.12, arm64, 10,240 MB, SnapStart) and what each costs. Each profiler arm runs P1's code with one profiler on; its cost is the difference in Lambda's own REPORT numbers against a REPORT-only control (rep), paired by round (and by request for warm), Graviton3 only, judged against rep2, a second byte-identical REPORT-only function, as the null. 'nvidia-spi' (the operator's word) is read as NVIDIA's tooling: nvidia-smi and Nsight Systems/Compute.

changed_variable.name: profiler
changed_variable.experiment: one of: P1 phase timers (none), cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, lkaisamp native sampler, X-Ray active tracing, Telemetry API extension

conclusion: Applicability (in Lambda): NVIDIA tools (nvidia-smi, nsys, ncu) are INAPPLICABLE because there is no GPU (no /dev/nvidia*, no PCI 0x10de, no driver or libraries; 7 environments, all Graviton3 0xd40). perf, eBPF, ptrace and py-spy --native are DENIED (EPERM; CapEff 0, seccomp filter, perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU). These WORK: P1 phase timers, REPORT/CloudWatch, X-Ray, the Telemetry API extension, cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, and an in-process SIGPROF sampler (lkaisamp), which gives native KleidiAI kernel profiles where perf is denied. Overhead (run 20261020T231634Z: 8 arms, 4,800 invocations, 0 errors, a fresh Lambda client per wave; mean of 5 per-round paired deltas vs rep on Graviton3, each arm tested against the rep2 same-code null by an exact permutation test, p<0.05 and beyond the null's largest |delta|): phase timers and X-Ray show no cost distinguishable from the null on any phase (null spread up to 28 ms Init, 155 ms cold Duration, 112 ms Restore Duration, 35 ms first restored request, ~1.8% warm). Measurable: cProfile +113 ms Init (14%); Telemetry extension +93 ms Init (11%); py-spy +4.7% median per warm request; lkaisamp +457 ms cold first-request Duration. lkaisamp's first-after-restore Duration rose +1.5 to +1.8 s in 3 of 5 rounds but not in 2, so it is not called measurable (p=0.119); the delta is outside the baseline's internal timing but before lkai_prof.handler returns, and attribution within its dump/symbolise hook remains open. Final latency comparisons should use REPORT or phase timers only. Hot spots (shares of all recorded samples): cold = S3 download 25.0 s (69.4%; 58% of py-spy init samples in TLS read) then the KleidiAI repack 8.4 s (23.3%; buffer_set_tensor 30.8% + rhs_pack 12.2% of init CPU samples, single-threaded offline). Restore = Lambda restore 3.21 s (82%), then a first forward 2.8x warm whose CPU samples are 51% memset inside llama_kv_cache::clear / llama_memory_recurrent::clear. Warm = KleidiAI i8mm matmul 49% of CPU, then f32 dot 9%, gated-delta-net 8%, concat 6%, OpenMP barrier 5%, fwht 5%. Run 20261020T124451Z is superseded: one pooled Lambda client across SnapStart waits lost 45 restore invokes to client timeouts (this was earlier misreported as a Lambda platform stall), and its noise floor was the X-Ray arm itself. Status is inconclusive because this is a measurement study, not a latency change.
